outcome_source.selection: params == '1B', final step (69369) per recipe/seed/task, metrics.primary_metric, 3 seeds (default, large aux 2, large aux 3) averaged; mmlu = DataDecide's macro average over the 57 subjects

rule: lower statistic predicts higher accuracy; pairs with |acc diff| < 2 x pooled seed SD dropped (pooled SD = sqrt(mean over recipes of the 3-seed variance), per task)

proxy_baseline.method: DataDecide single-scale ranking: final-checkpoint primary_metric of a small model, 3 seeds (default, small aux 2, small aux 3) averaged; same pinned parquet; scored on the same 1,660 noise-filtered 1B task-pairs (outcome: 1B primary_metric); higher proxy value predicts higher 1B accuracy
proxy_baseline.datadecide_reported: Magnusson et al. 2025 (DataDecide), abstract: ranking models at a single small size (e.g. 150M) predicts the best models at 1B with ~80% of comparisons correct. Their pair set (all recipe pairs, their target metric and aggregation) differs from ours (1,660 noise-filtered task-pairs).

proxy_baseline_continuous.method: DataDecide single-scale ranking: final-checkpoint correct_prob_per_char / total_prob_per_char of a small model, 3 seeds (default, small aux 2, small aux 3) averaged; same pinned parquet; scored on the same 1,660 noise-filtered 1B task-pairs (outcome: 1B primary_metric); higher proxy value predicts higher 1B accuracy
proxy_baseline_continuous.metric_choice: Primary: correct_prob_per_char. DataDecide (arXiv 2504.11393, sec. 3.3): 'Here we chose a single length normalization, *_per_char.' ... 'Using Correct Prob or Total Prob leads to decision accuracy at least as good as any other metric for most small scales.' Sec. 3.4: 'Using Correct Prob sees wider spreads or reduced noise for many tasks.' total_prob_per_char (co-recommended) is reported alongside, not as the primary.
